# Blazor

- BLZ-014 (must): Don't implement authorization checks in client-side code if enforcement must be guaranteed; always perform authorization checks on the server within any API endpoints a client-side app accesses. Don't store app secrets, connection strings, credentials, passwords, PINs, private .NET/C# code or private keys and tokens in client-side code.
- BLZ-017 (should): Components that use the interactive WebAssembly and Auto render modes should be designed so that they run successfully from both the client and the server. If such a component must call a server project-based API, or transform a request to an external web API, when running on the client, the recommended approach is to abstract that API call behind a service interface and implement client and server versions of the service.
